key_insight: Elastic frontogenesis creates thin, intensifying polymer-stress sheets whose geometry explains power-law spectra despite a spatially smooth velocity field.
engineering_relevance: This mechanism offers a framework for interpreting multiscale fluctuations in polymer-solution flows where inertia is negligible.
method: Identify sheet-like polymer-stress fronts stretched in-plane and compressed across their thickness.
Relate front amplification and thinning to the polymer conformation spectrum.
Use the Stokes response to connect this geometric scaling to the velocity spectrum.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust power-law spectra in velocity and polymer conformation but provides no numerical exponents, evaluation details, or quantitative validation.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish how broadly the proposed geometric scaling holds across constitutive models and flow conditions.
paper_title: Elastic frontogenesis sets the spectra of smooth elastic turbulence
